question.problem: Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨2y,\,2x,\,2z⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined in Cartesian coordinates as $z=2$ for $0\le x\le \frac{1}{2}$ and $0\le y\le \frac{1}{4}.$ Calculate the flux of $F$ through $S$ with respect to the *downward*-pointing unit normal vector $n.$
question.worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is a  continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

For the surface $z=1$ for  $0\le x\le \frac{1}{2}$ and $0\le y\le \frac{1}{4},$ the downward-pointing unit normal vector is

$$
n=⟨0,\,0,\,-1⟩.
$$

Using the fact that $z=2$ on $S,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨2y,\,2x,\,2z⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨2y,\,2x,\,4⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the flux of $F$ across $S$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}(-4)\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-4)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/4}{\int }_{0}^{1/2}(-4)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =-4{\int }_{0}^{1/4}\,\text{d}y{\int }_{0}^{1/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-4\cdot [y]_{0}^{1/4}\cdot [x]_{0}^{1/2} \\  & =-4\cdot \frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
